# Volume 3 — Chapter XXV Enter Prince Charming

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“I’m comparing what’s inside with what’s outside,” Nell said, her gaze shifting from Tabby’s Place’s window toward the park’s far-off pines.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0000 }

“Aunt Phemie, I have an entire afternoon to devote to pleasant idleness. Is it better to pass it in this spot, featuring a comfortable hearth, a dish piled with tasty russet apples, three purring, contented cats, and a pair of flawless porcelain dogs boasting green noses? Or should I head over to the park, drawn by the attraction of gray forests and gray waves splashing against the rocks of the harbor?”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0001 }

“I would choose the park if my age matched yours,” Aunt Euphemia remarked, using a knitting needle to tickle the yellow ear of Joseph.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0002 }

“Aunty, I believed you maintained that you were just as young as the rest of us,” Nell teased.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0003 }

“Indeed, within my spirit. However, I must concede that my legs lack the youth of your own. Head outside to catch some fresh air, Nell. Your complexion has appeared pale recently.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0004 }

“I believe I will head over to the park,” Nell stated impatiently. “Living room quietness does not appeal to me today. My desire is to feel solitary, unrestricted, and untamed. Nobody will be in the park, as all the people are going to attend the football match.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0005 }

“For what reason were you absent from it?”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0006 }

“‘Nobody axed me, sir, she said’—or at least, no one except that dreadful small Dan Ranger. I would not attend anything alongside him; however, instead of injuring his fragile little sensitive emotions, I stated that I was not attending the game whatsoever. It does not bother me. For some reason, I am simply not feeling up for football today.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0007 }

“Go out and breathe some fresh air,” Aunt Euphemia reiterated, “yet carry your umbrella with you, because I think rain is coming. My leg has rheumatism.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0008 }

“Rheumatism ought to be confined to the elderly, Aunty.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0009 }

“A person can easily catch rheumatism in her legs, Nell. However, solely the elderly ought to experience soul rheumatism. Fortunately, I have escaped it entirely. Once your soul is afflicted with rheumatism, you may as well proceed to select your coffin.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0010 }

November had arrived—that time of deep, melancholic ocean hymns, crimson sunsets, fierce wind-songs among the pines, and departing birds. Nell wandered along the pineland paths inside the park and, in her own words, allowed that huge, sweeping wind to clear the fogs from her soul. Normally, soul fog did not bother Nell. Yet, for some reason, ever since she had come back to Wexcombe to begin this third year, life no longer reflected her spirit with its former, flawless, brilliant clarity.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0011 }

On the surface, life at Tabby’s Place continued in its usual enjoyable cycle of labor, learning, and amusement. Every Friday night, many visitors filled the spacious, fire-lit livingroom, which resounded with continuous jokes and merriment, all under the radiant smile of Aunt Euphemia. The person named “Ezra” in Cressy’s letter visited frequently, taking the morning train from St. Columbia and leaving on the night train. Everyone at Tabby’s Place held him in high regard, even if Aunt Euphemia would shake her head and express her opinion that theology students had declined compared to former days.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0012 }

“My dear, he is extremely pleasant,” she remarked to Cressy, “yet it is necessary for ministers to possess greater gravity and dignity.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0013 }

“Is it impossible for someone to be a Christian while also indulging in laughter after laughter?” Cressy asked.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0014 }

“Oh, men—yes. However, it was of ministers that I was speaking, my dear,” Aunt Euphemia said in a rebuking manner. “Furthermore, you ought not to flirt in that way with Mr. Hale—you truly ought not to.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0015 }

“Flirting with him is not what I’m doing,” Cressy argued.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0016 }

Save for Nell, no one gave her credence. Believing she was merely entertaining herself as she so often did, the rest informed her bluntly that her conduct was extremely poor.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0017 }

“Cressy, Mr. Hale does not belong to the Hector-and-Orlando category,” Mabel stated sternly. “His approach to life is earnest. It is possible that you will break his heart.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0018 }

“Do you truly believe I would be capable of it?” Cressy inquired. “I would delight in believing that.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0019 }

“Cressida Lindsay! I never considered you completely heartless. To think you declared that you would delight in breaking a man’s heart!”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0020 }

“Honey, I never uttered those words. State what I said accurately. My statement was that I would prefer to believe I possessed the ability to shatter it. I wish to be certain that I held the strength required for such an act.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0021 }

“Cressy, you make no sense to me. It is obvious you are intentionally encouraging him, yet you are fully aware that your intentions are not serious.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0022 }

“If possible, I intend to get him to propose marriage to me,” Cressy stated composedly.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0023 }

“I surrender to you,” Mabel said with a sense of hopelessness.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0024 }

Hugh visited from time to time on Friday nights. He appeared to be perpetually cheerful, and he maintained his position during the swift exchange of jokes and witty remarks. He did not chase after Nell, nor did he evade her. Whenever situation placed them together, his conversation with her was agreeable and polite, just as it would be with a fresh acquaintance. Their previous closeness had vanished completely. Nell was deeply hurt by this; nevertheless, she assured herself that she felt immense joy and gratitude regarding how thoroughly Hugh had overcome his letdown concerning her. On that April night among the fruit trees, she had actually feared that she had wounded him severely and that his recovery would take a great deal of time. At present, she perceived that her anxiety had been unnecessary. Men have died and the worms have eaten them but not for love. Clearly, Hugh faced no threat of an early death. He was taking pleasure in living, and he possessed an abundance of drive and enthusiasm. As for him, he would not pine away in misery simply because a lady was beautiful and indifferent. Nell, while hearing the unending teasing that transpired between him and Cressy, questioned whether she had merely pictured that expression in his eyes on the occasion when she informed him that she could not ever love him.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0025 }

Individuals were not absent who would have willingly taken the empty spot of Hugh. Nell, however, dismissed them devoid of fear and devoid of reproach. Should the genuine Prince Charming fail to ever arrive, she refused to accept any replacement. Thus she rigidly informed herself on that gloomy day within the breezy park.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0026 }

Aunt Euphemia’s prophesied rain abruptly arrived with a swish and rush. Raising her umbrella, Nell hastened down the slope. A fierce gust of wind swept along the harbor road just as she turned onto it. Her umbrella immediately turned wrong side out. Nell made a desperate grab at it. And then—a voice spoke right beside her.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0027 }

“Excuse me—could I provide you cover with my umbrella?”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0028 }

Nell raised her eyes. Standing right in front of her in real life was the exact protagonist of her fantasies—lofty, attractive, and dignified, possessing dark, somber, unfathomable eyes, alongside a tender, melodic, compassionate tone. Had he been created to specification, he could not have matched her perfection more accurately.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0029 }

“Thank you,” she uttered, feeling bewildered.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0030 }

“It would be best if we made haste to that small pavilion on the point,” the stranger proposed. “There we can bide our time till this downpour ceases. Such intense rain is improbable to persist for much longer.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0031 }

Although the spoken phrasing was extremely ordinary, the voice held such a distinct quality, matched by her expression as she uttered them, that Nell experienced a curious fluttering in her chest.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0032 }

They hurried as one to the pavilion and settled breathlessly beneath its welcoming shelter. Displaying her imitation umbrella, Nell laughed.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0033 }

“I become certain that non-living objects are completely evil the moment my umbrella gets blown inside out,” she remarked cheerfully.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0034 }

Glistening drops of rain gleamed on her glossy hair, whose untethered tresses coiled about her forehead and neck. Glowing cheeks accompanied her wide, luminous eyes. Looking down, her associate regarded her with admiration. His look made her feel her face redden. What was his identity? Look, a fragment of the Wexcombe scarlet and white was attached to his coat lapel. Still, she had believed she was familiar with, at minimum by appearance, every one of the Wexcombe students apart from the Freshmen. And this polite young man certainly was not a Freshman.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0035 }

“I see that we are schoolmates,” he stated, offering a smile toward Nell’s colors. “That should serve as a sufficient introduction. Royal Lisle is my name. And aren't you the Miss Harcourt who delivered the Tennyson paper at the Philomathic just the other evening?”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0036 }

“Indeed; however, I am unable to place you whatsoever,” Nell admitted candidly. “Pray, what is your origin?”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0037 }

“I have the impression that I do not fit in anywhere so far. Two years back, I completed my Freshman and Sophomore years at Wexcombe. I have resided in Europe from that time onward. At present, I have returned so that I can complete my Arts degree.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0038 }

“I am also in my Junior year,” Nell said.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0039 }

“Then we share a class in addition to sharing a college. I am resigned to losing the years destroyed by the locust,” her partner remarked, a universe of significance filling those extraordinary eyes he possessed.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0040 }

The rain fell without ceasing for almost an hour. Nevertheless, the duration appeared remarkably brief. Nell and her associate journeyed home side by side when the clouds split open and a ray of faint November sunlight swept across the harbor and the pines. Before they arrived at the gate of Tabby’s Place he had requested consent to visit, and it had been granted to him. Nell entered with glowing cheeks, her heart throbbing all the way to her fingertips. Smudge, who scrambled onto her lap attempting to lick her, received a most distracted greeting. Nell, her spirit completely filled with romantic excitement, possessed no focus to bestow upon a crop-eared pussy cat at that moment.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0041 }

During that same evening, a package was delivered to Tabby’s Place, addressed to Miss Harcourt. Within the box were twelve splendid roses. Cressy boldly seized the card that dropped out, reading both the name and the verse of poetry inscribed upon its reverse side.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0042 }

“Royal Lisle!” she cried out. “Why, Nell, I wasn’t aware that Cyril Lisle was an acquaintance of yours!”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0043 }

“I encountered him in the park during the rain this afternoon,” Nell explained hastily. “His umbrella was used to rescue me when mine flipped inside out.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0044 }

“Oh!” Cressy took a curious look at Nell. “Does such an exceptionally ordinary event explain his sending us long-stemmed roses by the dozen, accompanied by a highly sentimental poem? Or explain our flushing the most divine rosy-red upon viewing his card? Nell, your face gives you away.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0045 }

“Stop speaking absurdities, Cressy. Are you acquainted with Mr. Lisle?”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0046 }

“I have gotten to know his couple of sisters, and I am aware of him. Everyone of any importance in Portmaris is, too. Among the wealthiest, most elite of Bluenoses are the Gardners. Cyril possesses endearing good looks and intelligence. His mother’s wellness broke down two years back, forcing him to quit university and travel overseas alongside her—his father has passed away. Having to abandon his year must have caused him deep disappointment, yet people claim he acted entirely wonderfully concerning the matter. Fee—fi—fo—fum, Nell. Romance is in the air. I nearly feel jealous of you, though not entirely. When all is said and done, Cyril Lisle cannot compare to Ezra.”
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0047 }

“You goose!” Nell said in a lofty manner. Nevertheless, she remained awake for a considerable time that night, without any desire to sleep. The thoughts of her waking hours held far greater allure than any dreamland vision. Was this, finally, the arrival of the true Prince? As Nell remembered those magnificent dark eyes that had looked so intently into hers, she felt a powerful urge to believe that he had indeed arrived.
{: #nw-v03-c25-p0048 }
